title: Gold semantic benchmark for the template planner
description: Thirty-two synthetic business cases with concept-level gold bindings, forbidden paths, required blocks and a fixed calibration/holdout split. No Docentric corpus content is used.
split_policy: The split was fixed before the first live run. Calibration cases may be used to tune prompts or routing; holdout cases must not be used for tuning and are reported separately.

provenance.author: v0.10 single annotator (implementer)
notes: Author labels are preserved; the independent adjudicator reproduced them or flagged a documented disagreement.
The adjudicator is a deterministic proxy, not a second human annotator. AT-07 remains partial.
Image-family adjudication: all three committed image cases are expressible at the annotated company-logo path; label_status=verified, no case excluded as a gap.

cases.prompt: Create a line table with item, description, quantity, unit, unit price, discount percent, net amount, tax amount, line amount, warehouse, delivery date and line note.

cases.prompt: Create a quotation line table with item number, description, quantity and line amount for every line; the table must handle forty rows.
cases.notes: The fixture carries forty sample rows; the prompt tests that the model keeps the collection repeat rather than a fixed row count.

cases.prompt: Create a line table with item number, the long description and line amount; keep the description column wide enough for long text.
cases.notes: Long descriptions are a layout concern, but the semantic binding must still target the description field.

cases.prompt: Show the VAT number on the quotation.

required_bindings.note: The prompt does not say whose VAT number; both parties are defensible.

cases.notes: Genuine ambiguity between customer and company VAT numbers; the alternative is accepted, not guessed.

cases.prompt: Create a service order with a table of service lines showing the line description and, under each line, a nested list of tasks showing the task id, description and hours.
cases.notes: Nested repeat scope: the line description and the task fields use the outer and inner collection respectively; the task fields must not use the outer line scope.

cases.prompt: Create a service order table showing each service line's item number and, nested beneath it, each task's id, rate and amount.
cases.notes: Nested list with money fields; the outer line table and the inner task repeat must both use the correct collection scope.

cases.prompt: Create a service order table with line item, line amount and a nested list of task description and hours.
cases.notes: A second nested composition; differs from the first by mixing line amount with task text/effort.

cases.prompt: Create a quotation with the customer name and a VAT notice that only appears when the customer is in the EU.
cases.notes: The schema has a separate Parameters.ShowVatNotice flag; the prompt conditions on the customer's EU status, so the flag is forbidden.

cases.prompt: Create a tax invoice with a reverse-charge notice that appears only when reverse charge is enabled, and show the tax amount and gross amount.
cases.notes: A boolean condition plus two monetary fields; reverse charge must drive the condition.

cases.prompt: If the customer is in the EU, show a VAT notice and the customer VAT number; always show the invoice total.
cases.notes: Conditional VAT rendering on the invoice fixture; the total stays unconditional.
